method: Pictures first: looked at the overview, rendered the whole level (L1_full, grid 1), then 15 tiles of 5x5 m (grid 0.5, --inserts --text, 2000 px), row by row: A x-6.6..-1.6 / B x-2.2..2.8 / C x2.2..7.2 at y-10..-5; D/E/F at y-5.5..-0.5; G/H/I at y-1..4; J/K/L at y3.5..8.5; M/N/O at y8..13. Added close-ups of the toilet and stair hall (x0.8..4.6, y6.6..10.2) and the east ATM slot. Then I checked every candidate against the geometry in prims.pkl: A-WALL, A-WALL-PATT and S-COLS hatch loops (wall and column outlines), the lines of the 11 'Basic Wall _ GLASS WALL' blocks, the A-GLAZ-CURT panels and A-GLAZ-CWMG mullions, and all 16 A-DOOR inserts with their A-DOOR-FRAM frames, leaves and arcs, plus the A-FLOR threshold lines. Caution: in prims, insert points of mirrored blocks (sy=-1) have x negated (OCS), so I used the exploded geometry instead of those points. I built a filled 'solids' map (walls black, columns grey, glass cyan, frames red) so every wall gap stands out. Every door insert point turned out to be exactly the midpoint of its gap, which confirms the ends. Where a and b go: on the wall centre line at the wall-end faces, frame included. For doors in curtain walls, at the inner faces of the flanking mullions. For doors in GLASS WALL partitions, at the ends of the partition elements, so the 25 mm jamb mullions are included. Results: 16 A-DOOR blocks give 15 door openings (the two SE pivot blocks share one slot), plus one doorless passage (B1-14). No window blocks exist on L1. The facade curtain walls and the glazed partitions are listed as glassWalls. To verify, I drew every opening as a segment and marker on the solids map and the normal render: the whole level, then 7 zooms (east doors, SE entrance, back lobby, manager door, north corridor, lift hall, NE toilet), plus a glass-wall check. Every swing, leaf, door block and wall gap is now either an opening, a column-filled gap or a listed rejection. All scripts and outputs are in the label-bank-L1-B folder; the full key is answer_key_bank_L1_B.json.
